activity_context.topic_title: Properties of Line Integrals With Respect to X and Y

examples.problem: If $\displaystyle\int_{C} f(x,y) \,\textrm d x= 8$ and $\displaystyle\int_{-C_1} f(x,y) \,\textrm d x= -2,$ calculate $\displaystyle\int_{-C_2} f(x,y) \,\textrm d x$ given that $C = C_1\cup C_2.$
examples.worked_solution:
Let $C = C_1\cup C_2$ be a piecewise smooth path in the $xy$-plane, and let $-C$ be the curve consisting of the same points as $C$ but with the opposite orientation. 

For line integrals with respect to $x,$ we have the following properties:

- $\displaystyle\int_{-C} f(x,y)\,\textrm d x = -\int_{C} f(x,y)\,\textrm d x$

- $\displaystyle\int_{C} f(x,y)\,\textrm d x = \int_{C_1} f(x,y)\,\textrm d x + \int_{C_2} f(x,y)\,\textrm d x$

In our case, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{{C}_{1}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x \\ 8 & =-{\int }_{-{C}_{1}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x-{\int }_{-{C}_{2}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x \\ 8 & =-(-2)-{\int }_{-{C}_{2}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x \\ 8 & =2-{\int }_{-{C}_{2}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x \\ 6 & =-{\int }_{-{C}_{2}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\int_{-C_2} f(x,y) \,\textrm d x = -6.
$$

feedback.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14059897/assets/2400f92070b4f7d4e0ad0309574b729da86754bc64b6d7a3c508433d1bbc7f76.png)

Calculate ${\int }_{C}\,\text{d}y,$ where $C$ is the path along the line segment between the points $(4,0)$ to the point $(0,3),$ as shown above.
feedback.worked_solution:
The line integral of unity with respect to $y$ along a path $C$ is equal to the net change in $y$ between the terminal and initial points:

$$
{\int }_{C}\,\text{d}y={y}_{2}-{y}_{1},
$$

where ${y}_{2}$ is the $y$-coordinate of the terminal point, and ${y}_{1}$ is the $y$-coordinate of the initial point.

In our case, ${y}_{2}=3$ and ${y}_{1}=0.$ Therefore,

$$
{\int }_{C}\,\text{d}y={y}_{2}-{y}_{1}=3-0=3.
$$
